extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and examiner trainees (and patent prosecutors/attorneys reading written-description guidance)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examining patent applications for compliance with the written description requirement of 35 U.S.C. § 112, first paragraph, including how to compare claim scope to specification, assess possession by one skilled in the art, and handle amended/priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine what the claim as a whole covers
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination as to what the claim as a whole covers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In making this determination, the examiner should consider and discuss the full scope of the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare claim scope with disclosure in the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: A full review of the application to understand how the applicant provides support for the claimed invention including each element and/or step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This review includes comparing the claim scope with the scope of the description; for amended claims compare scope to original claims and the specification (see decision trees in Appendices B and C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Possession by one skilled in the art
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination as to whether one skilled in the art would recognize that the applicant was in possession of the claimed invention as a whole at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This determination should include consideration of: actual reduction to practice; disclosure of drawings or structural chemical formulas; sufficient relevant identifying characteristics (complete structure, partial structure, physical and/or chemical properties, functional characteristics when coupled with a known or disclosed correlation between function and structure); method of making the claimed invention; level of skill and knowledge in the art; predictability in the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration for single-embodiment/species claims
rubrics_metrics.description: For each claim drawn to a single embodiment or species, consider whether one of ordinary skill in the art would recognize that the applicant was in possession of that embodiment or species at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same factors listed under 'Possession by one skilled in the art' specifically to the disclosed embodiment/species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration for genus claims (representative species requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each claim drawn to a genus, determine whether there is disclosure of a representative number of species which would lead one skilled in the art to conclude that the applicant was in possession of the claimed genus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number of species required to represent a genus will vary depending on the level of skill and knowledge in the art and the variability among the claimed genus: fewer species are required where skill and knowledge are high; more where the genus is highly variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of transitional/open vs closed claim language
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand how transitional phrases affect claim scope (e.g., 'comprising' vs 'consisting of').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open transitional language ('comprising') may claim a genus that includes additional sequences or elements (broader scope); closed transitional language ('consisting of') limits the claim to the single species expressly recited. This affects whether the specification's disclosure of a single species supports the full claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess whether missing/omitted element makes amended claim broader than original
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims are amended to remove a limitation, determine whether the amendment results in a claim broader than the original claim and whether the specification supports the broader scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the decision tree where no benefit claimed (Appendix B) or where benefit claimed (Appendix C). If the missing element was a critical feature described in the specification, omission likely renders the amended claim unsupported by the specification (written description failure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical feature analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether a feature omitted from a claim (or absent from the parent) is described in the specification as critical to proper functioning of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the specification describes a feature as critical (e.g., shape is critical to function) then disclosure of only that species will not show possession of a broader genus; the broader claim is not entitled to the earlier filing date and fails written description for that scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of functional/flow-chart/software disclosure when supported by conventional hardware
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether a specification that provides detailed functional flow diagrams or steps (but not source code) sufficiently describes the claimed computer-implemented invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosing conventional hardware (e.g., a microprocessor capable of performing the functions) plus a detailed functional description/drawings can be sufficient for written description where one skilled in the art would understand what's being described and recognize the inventor was in possession of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative species via shared structural feature (e.g., SEQ ID)
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosed species that provides a structural feature common to members of a claimed genus may be representative of the genus if the complete structure of that common feature is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claimed genus is defined by the presence of a particular structural element (e.g., a specific EST sequence) and the specification discloses the complete sequence, that species may be representative and support the genus when one skilled in the art can add flanking sequences by routine experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of identifying characteristics for proteins
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether identifying characteristics provided in the specification (partial amino acid sequence, functional activity, molecular weight, purification data, method of isolation) are sufficient to show possession of the claimed protein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial sequence plus functional data and an isolation/production method can be sufficient for written description of a protein claim if a person skilled in the art would recognize possession of the claimed protein from those identifying characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of identifying characteristics for DNAs encoding proteins
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether disclosure supports claims to DNAs encoding a protein when the specification gives only partial protein sequence or other protein characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial protein sequence and protein characteristics may not provide sufficient identifying information about the DNA (e.g., size alone is insufficient). Disclosure of a method to obtain the DNA or cloning/isolation of the DNA (or deposited DNA) strengthens written description support; percentage of structure disclosed (e.g., % of amino-acid sequence) is relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider presence or absence of art-recognized structure–function correlation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether an art-recognized correlation between structure and function exists and is disclosed in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a known structure–function correlation is disclosed (or exists in the art), functional claims or claims based on partial structure may be better supported; absent such correlation, functional language is less likely to show possession of broad genus/species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider level of ordinary skill and predictability in the art
rubrics_metrics.description: Take into account the level of skill and knowledge in the art and how predictable the art is when assessing whether disclosure demonstrates possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher skill and predictability reduce the number/amount of species or detail needed to support a genus; lower skill or unpredictability require more detailed/species disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use USPTO decision trees for amended/priority-benefit claim analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the procedural decision trees provided in Appendix B (no benefit claimed) and Appendix C (benefit claimed) to determine entitlement to earlier filing dates and written-description outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These decision trees direct examiners to compare amended/amending claims to original claims and specification, evaluate missing elements and criticality, and then decide written description and entitlement issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate consideration of enablement, utility, and prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that written description analysis is distinct from enablement, utility, and novelty/anticipation issues, though those issues should be considered during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The training materials note that other rejections (e.g., lack of enablement, lack of patentable utility, anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102) may be appropriate even when written description is satisfied; examiners should make other rejections where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of reduction to practice and methods of making
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the specification provides an actual reduction to practice or a method for making the claimed invention, as evidence of possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual working examples, procedures for isolation or synthesis, and concrete production steps strengthen written description support; their absence weighs against possession, especially for broad claims.
